Definition: of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans):--murderer. Compare G5406.
BiblicalUsage: Sikarios is a dagger-man, an assassin, and it appears once, when the Roman commander mistakes Paul for the Egyptian who led four thousand murderers into the wilderness. The word is the Roman name for the Jewish fanatics who killed with hidden daggers.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the commander's mistake shows how little Rome understood the Jews, and how easily a preacher of peace is taken for a man of violence.
